<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via resolvePredicateRelated (symbol, a method of class ObjectQL))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via cascadeDeleteRelations (symbol, a method of class ObjectQL))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9d81af714f4938f368909322ac8eb2c24276598a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `263c6c0f53b8d24faf6c4f5137b7c944beebdbfc` — the merge of head `b22174cd4da742de304d22523c36462870f64ce8` into base `9d81af714f4938f368909322ac8eb2c24276598a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 263c6c0f53b8d24faf6c4f5137b7c944beebdbfc && git checkout 263c6c0f53b8d24faf6c4f5137b7c944beebdbfc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9d81af714f4938f368909322ac8eb2c24276598a b22174cd4da742de304d22523c36462870f64ce8 && git checkout -B drift-repro 9d81af714f4938f368909322ac8eb2c24276598a && git merge --no-ff b22174cd4da742de304d22523c36462870f64ce8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9d81af714f4938f368909322ac8eb2c24276598a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9d81af714f4938f368909322ac8eb2c24276598a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b1de69f917de0629e5d1c3789aad360e44ada51e`

Scope read:
- card #20006, body and 3 comments (the os-dev report is treated as a claim);
- #18682 records `5790469129` (round-11 Q1, options A–D verbatim), `5792704279` and `5795813514`;
- the PR body, and the whole diff `fc6ddb87a..b1de69f91` (5 files);
- AGENTS.md (Prime Directives, the runtime-strings rule) and `contract-review.md`;
- at head: `rule-validator.ts`, `engine.ts` (`resolvePredicateRelated`, `cascadeDeleteRelations`), `operation-private-keys.ts`, `ENTRY_EXECUTION_CONTEXT_FIELDS`, `field.zod.ts` `deleteBehavior`, and plugin-security's `delete-reference-cleanup-system-identity.test.ts`.

Run in the reviewer's own detached worktree at head, which was removed afterwards:
- the two pin files (63/63), the plugin-security fixture (18/18), and eslint over the 4 touched files (0/0);
- a probe of 14 delete shapes, 12 write shapes and 7 multi-value shapes, run at head AND with both source files reverted to the merge base;
- the built d.ts.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The refused set is unchanged: RIGHT.** Over the 14 delete shapes, base and head give identical verdicts, and `code` + `fields[]` (whole `constraint`) are byte-identical. `record.amount > 100 && record.account.status == 'closed'` (amount 50) and a `has(record.account.status)`-guarded rule pass the cleanup at base and at head. The 12 ordinary writes and 7 multi-value shapes are identical too. The refusal stays fail-closed.
- **Option D's literal mechanism is rejected: RIGHT.**
  - Option D (`5790469129`) reads: "hand an explicit unavailable binding … needs a new RelatedUnavailableReason member, which is a public type".
  - `resolveTraversalScope` refuses before evaluation on any absent binding, so D's literal mechanism would refuse the two shapes above, which is a narrowing. `RelatedUnavailableReason` is in the published d.ts.
  - The ruled direction, 「让外键清空的拒绝文字指对对象」, is implemented on the fault path instead.
- **The error envelope is unchanged: RIGHT.** `VALIDATION_FAILED`, `rule_violation`, `_record` and `constraint {rule, reason:'unevaluable', fault, missingKey}` are byte-identical in every refused shape. Only `message` differs, and only in the cleanup shapes.
- **The new text is reached only on the right write: RIGHT, with one corner (③ F1).**
  - The cause is read at one site, inside the pre-existing `__referentialFieldClear` branch, and handed only to the row matching `referencingId` on `referencingObject`.
  - These keep today's text (measured): an inherited context on another row, a hand-emptied reference, an own-column fault (`record.nope`), and ordinary writes.
- **SECURITY / disclosure: RIGHT, nothing new.**
  - The cleanup UPDATE runs under the deleter's own identity, exempt only from the object-level CRUD check. Only the pre-delete probe runs as system.
  - The new text names the parent object and id (the caller supplied both), the child object, the reference field, the rule name and the traversed column. Each was already disclosed by the old text, `constraint`, or the sibling restrict path (ruling #12166 c2, `err.dependentObject`). No count is disclosed.
  - The referencing row's id never reaches the text (measured).
  - A cleanup of a row the deleter cannot write is refused earlier with `PERMISSION_DENIED`. The #18682 secret/public equivalence pin is green.
  - The cause cannot be forged from REST: the entry context list is closed, with no `__` key, and forwarding consumers strip the `__` prefix. It authorizes nothing.
- **The prescriptions are true: RIGHT, with an undisclosed cost (③ F2).**
  - The guard makes the same delete succeed. An ordinary write with the reference set still refuses with the authored message.
  - `deleteBehavior` is `z.enum(['set_null','cascade','restrict'])` on `FieldSchema`. `cascade` deletes the child and `restrict` gives `DELETE_RESTRICTED` 409, measured on single- and multi-value references.
  - Offering only `deleteBehavior` for multi-value references is right: the cleanup keeps the other members, so the guard would still run the rule (measured: still refused).
- **Public surface: RIGHT.** The new names have 0 hits in the built `index.d.ts`, `core.d.ts` and util chunk (control: `RelatedRecordBinding` has 1/1/3). There is no new error code. `update()` and `OperationContext` are untouched. There is no tracker number in the runtime string.
- **Ablation: RIGHT.** Both files reverted to base give 7 red of 68: the 3 new-text pins and the 4 evaluator pins. The other #20006 pins measure existing behaviour and stay green.
- **CI at head:** 34 runs, 31 success, 3 skipped (`Console Pin Gate`, `Build Docs`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`), 0 failures. Every required context is `success`.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/objectql: patch` with `Clause-②: no` is correct. A runtime message changes, while the accept set is measured unchanged, the envelope is byte-identical, and no reachable type, option, export or error code moves.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Changeset:** every sentence is TRUE, including the example block, which equals the generated message at head, with ONE exception. Bullet 3, "**Unchanged:** a rule whose fault is in its own columns … keep today's text byte for byte", is **FALSE in a measured shape (F1)**.

**Shipped refusal text at head:** every sentence of the single-value and multi-value forms is TRUE. The guard sentence is true as a repair for the delete, but silent about its cost (F2).

**F1: attribution by key name misfires on a name collision.**
- The case: `record.status == 'x' && record.account.status == 'closed'` on a `crm_deal` that declares no `status`. CEL faults on the bare `record.status`, with the same fault at base.
- Head nevertheless emits the cleanup text, because a missing key that is ALSO read through a reference is attributed to the reference.
- The rule is broken on every write, not by the cleanup. So the changeset's "Unchanged" bullet and the PR body's "A fault on the rule's own columns keeps the generic text" are false for this shape.

**F2: the guard silently stops enforcing a rule that reads ANOTHER reference.**
- Following "Guard the rule on `account` being set" for `record.region.kind == 'secret'` makes that rule skip every `crm_deal` whose `account` is empty, on every insert and update.
- Measured: a guarded rule on an account-less deal with a secret region is accepted; unguarded, it is refused.
- The text says only "still judged on every write where the reference is set". An author following a prescription must be told what it costs (PD #10).

**PR body:** TRUE where measured, including the option-D argument, the untouched `OperationContext` / `update()`, the d.ts counts, eslint, plugin-security 18/18, the `__`-prefix stripping, and "row id never reaches the text". The failing-probe-first count and the per-ablation counts are UNMEASURED; the reviewer's full revert is consistent. The #20007 reuse note is TRUE: `referenceGuardRepair(field)` is module-local in the same file. #20007 should carry F2's cost clause where it applies.

**Out-of-scope finding: REAL.** Through `ExpressionEngine.evaluate`, all seven `ConditionalValidationSchema` TSDoc example predicates in `packages/spec/src/data/validation.zod.ts` fail when copied: six give `parse: Unexpected character: =`, and `order_total > 10000` gives `Unknown variable`. The strings ship in the spec d.ts.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-20006-cascade-fk-clear-refusal-text`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Bvd69VPa6puiNzzPUroDBx`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

What must change (small, and both in files the claim already owns):
1. **F1.** Choose one:
   - tighten the attribution, so that a missing key that is also read bare at the root (`record.KEY`) keeps the generic text, pinned with `record.status == 'x' && record.account.status == 'closed'` on an object declaring no `status`;
   - or narrow the changeset bullet and the PR body to what the code does.
2. **F2.** Where the rule reads a DIFFERENT reference, state the guard's cost in the text and in the changeset bullet "It applies whether…", e.g. "(the rule is then not judged on crm_deal records whose `account` is empty)". Or offer only `deleteBehavior` in that arm. Pin the account-less ordinary write in whichever direction the text promises.

Isolated reviewer: a contract-review-tier subagent, fed only the card, the #18682 records, the PR and AGENTS.md; adopted by the seat.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9a31fc9925e5a930aa5ae2a7c51b766a9883c448`

Scope read:
- card #20006, body and 4 comments (the round-1 os-dev addendum `5821932496` is treated as a claim), and the round-0 record `5821350148` in full;
- the PR body, including "Patch round 1";
- the diff `b1de69f91..9a31fc992` in full. It touches exactly `rule-validator.ts`, the two pin files and the changeset; `engine.ts` is untouched, and the merge base is still `fc6ddb87a`;
- at head: `rule-validator.ts` (`readsKeyOffTheTraversal`, `referentialClearRefusal`, `checkPredicate`), `declared-fields.ts`, `engine.ts` (`resolvePredicateRelated`), formula's `relationship-traversal.ts`, AGENTS.md and `contract-review.md`.

Run in the reviewer's own detached worktree at head, which was removed afterwards:
- the two pin files and the plugin-security fixture;
- a probe of 82 engine-level shapes (55 deletes, 27 ordinary writes) plus 8 evaluator-level shapes, run at head AND with `rule-validator.ts` + `engine.ts` reverted to `fc6ddb87a`;
- the same pins with `rule-validator.ts` reverted to `b1de69f91`;
- the built d.ts.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Diff scope: RIGHT.** Only the four files changed, so the round-0 measurements of `engine.ts` carry over.
- **F1, `readsKeyOffTheTraversal`: RIGHT on every shape the prior record asked for, WRONG on a neighbouring one (③ F3).**
  - `record.status == 'x' && record.account.status == 'closed'` on a `crm_deal` declaring no `status`: today's generic text byte for byte.
  - The same rule with `status` declared: stored null, absent or `'y'` is ACCEPTED, as at base. Stored `'x'` gives the cleanup text, every sentence of which is true: the declared read is materialised and cannot fault.
  - "which this object does not declare" is never emitted on a declared key.
  - The `||`, `previous.status`, `previous.kind == 'x' && record.region.kind == 'secret'` and json-field (`record.meta.status`) variants were all measured and behave as claimed.
  - A rule reading only through the cleared reference keeps the cleanup text.
- **F2, the guard's cost: RIGHT.**
  - The guard is offered only to a rule reading through the cleared reference. A rule reading only `record.region.kind` gets `deleteBehavior` alone, with no `conditional` in the text.
  - A rule reading BOTH references keeps the guard. Measured on insert (account omitted, explicit null, system and acting caller) and on update (set to null; already account-less): unguarded, every such write is refused before evaluation with `no single related record`, at base and at head. Guarded, those writes are accepted, and a write with `account` set is still judged.
  - So "already refuses every write that leaves that reference empty" is true.
- **Refused set: unchanged, RIGHT.** 0 verdicts moved between base and head over the 82 engine-level shapes. The pass-through controls pass at both.
- **Envelope: byte-identical, RIGHT.** `code`, `status`, the field error and the whole `constraint` are identical in all 82 shapes. Only `message` differs, in 22 cleanup refusals; three of those are ③ F3.
- **Public surface: RIGHT.** The five new module-local names have 0 hits in the built d.ts (controls 1/1/3), and there is no new error code.
- **Pins red then green: RIGHT.** Head's pin files against round 0's `rule-validator.ts` give 4 failed / 62 passed, exactly the four the addendum names. At head, 66/66. The plugin-security fixture is 18/18.
- **Disclosure:** nothing new.
- **CI at this head:** 41 runs, 0 failures, 0 pending. Every required context is `success`.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/objectql: patch` with `Clause-②: no` still holds.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Changeset:** every sentence is TRUE, including the example block, the guard bullet, the other-reference bullet and the multi-value bullet, EXCEPT the "Unchanged" bullet's sentence: "a rule whose fault is its own keeps today's text byte for byte. That covers a key the rule reads from `record` or `previous` directly, or through a field that is not a reference, which the record does not hold, even when the rule also reads a column of that name through a reference." It is **FALSE in a measured shape (F3)**.

**Shipped refusal texts at head:** every sentence is TRUE, in the single-value form (cleared reference), the other-reference form and the multi-value form.

**F3: attribution still keys on the ONE key CEL reports.**
- Measured on this CEL front end: when both operands of `&&` or `||` fault, the RIGHT operand's key is reported.
- So `record.kind == 'x' && record.account.status == 'closed'` on a `crm_deal` declaring no `kind` gets the cleanup text with the guard on the cleanup; base gave the generic text. The `||` form and `previous.kind == 'x' && record.account.status == 'closed'` do the same.
- With the operands swapped, each keeps the generic text. The outcome depends on operand order, not on where the rule is broken.
- The rule is broken on every write: an ordinary update with `account` set refuses with `No such key: kind … which this object does not declare`. Following the guard makes the delete succeed (measured), and the next linked write still faults on `kind`. The deleter is sent to a repair that hides the author's breakage.

**PR body:**
- "Patch round 1" is TRUE where measured. The ablation counts are UNMEASURED.
- The "How" bullet's description of `readsKeyOffTheTraversal` is **inaccurate for the `previous` root**: the code counts a reference hop on `previous` too (`skipReferences: false`). The function's own doc comment says so correctly.
- "A fault on the rule's own columns keeps the generic text" is FALSE (F3).

**`reuse_sentence_for_20007`: TRUE.** The guard sentence is unchanged, and #20007's `no single related record` arm needs no cost clause.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-20006-cascade-fk-clear-refusal-text`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Bvd69VPa6puiNzzPUroDBx`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

What must change (one item, in files the claim already owns):
1. **F3.** Either:
   - make the attribution answer for EVERY own read the rule makes, not only the reported key: any `record.K` the record does not hold, any `previous.K` the previous row does not hold, and any `record.F.K` / `previous.F.K` through a non-reference field whose value lacks `K`. Pinned with `record.kind == 'x' && record.account.status == 'closed'` (`kind` undeclared) on the cleanup, expecting today's text byte for byte, plus its ordinary-write control and the `||` and `previous.kind` legs;
   - or narrow the changeset's "Unchanged" bullet and the PR body to what the code does.

   Either way, the PR body's "How" description of the `previous` branch must be corrected (the seat edits the body).

Isolated reviewer: a contract-review-tier subagent, second read on this PR, fed only the card, the round-0 record, the PR and the two rule files; adopted by the seat.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b22174cd4da742de304d22523c36462870f64ce8`

Scope read:
- card #20006, body and all 5 comments (the round-2 addendum `5822695875` is treated as a claim), and the prior records `5821350148` and `5822275989` in full;
- the PR body, including "Patch round 2" and the rewritten "How" bullet;
- the diff `9a31fc992..b22174cd4`: 3 commits touching exactly `rule-validator.ts`, `engine-predicate-relationship.test.ts` and the changeset. `engine.ts` has been untouched since round 0, and the merge base is still `fc6ddb87a`;
- AGENTS.md (runtime-strings rule, PD #10) and `contract-review.md`, and the rule-validator / engine / formula code at head.

Run in the reviewer's own detached worktree at head, which was removed afterwards:
- the two pin files and the plugin-security fixture;
- the pin files with `9a31fc992`'s `rule-validator.ts` swapped in;
- a probe of 78 engine-level shapes (57 deletes, 21 ordinary writes), run at head AND with `rule-validator.ts` + `engine.ts` reverted to `fc6ddb87a`, plus 2 multi-value `deleteBehavior` shapes and an analyzer probe of 19 predicate sources;
- objectql's d.ts built with tsup at base and at head, compared byte for byte.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Diff scope since the last record: RIGHT.** Only the three files named, as a fast-forward.
- **F3, `readsAnOwnColumnItLacks`: RIGHT on every shape asked, and on every neighbouring shape hunted.**
  - `record.kind == 'x' && record.account.status == 'closed'` (`kind` undeclared), its `||` form and `previous.kind == 'x' && …` get today's generic text, byte for byte equal to the merge base. With the operands swapped, they are also generic and byte-equal to base.
  - With `kind` declared and stored `'x'`, they get the cleanup text with the guard, and every sentence of it is true.
  - A json field lacking the key, and `previous.F.K` through a reference hop, give generic text byte-identical to base.
  - A rule reading only through the cleared reference gets the cleanup text.
  - Also generic and byte-identical to base: a ternary, `size()`, `.startsWith()` and `in` on an undeclared own key, the collisions, `record.nope` alone, and the pre-evaluation refusals.
  - **Hunt 1, the cleanup text for a rule whose fault is its own:** none found among own reads.
  - **Hunt 2, a generic text that now says something false:** none. Every generic message at head is byte-identical to base's.
- **Regression against the prior records' passes: RIGHT.**
  - F1's shapes hold.
  - F2: the guard goes only to the cleared reference, the other reference gets `deleteBehavior` alone, and the both-references rule keeps the guard. The account-less direction was measured.
  - Multi-value: the text, `deleteBehavior` only, the guard still running the rule, and `cascade` / `restrict` were all measured.
- **Refused set: unchanged, RIGHT.** 0 of 78 verdicts moved between base and head, and the pass-throughs are accepted at both.
- **Envelope: byte-identical, RIGHT.** `code`, `status`, the field error and the whole `constraint` are identical in all 78 shapes. Only `message` differs, in 18 delete cleanups where only the traversal faults, plus the PR's own forged-marker control.
- **Public surface: RIGHT.** `index.d.ts`, `core.d.ts` and the util chunk built at base and at head are BYTE-IDENTICAL (180902 / 15039 / 553276 bytes). There is no new error code, and no tracker number in any runtime string.
- **Pins red then green: RIGHT.** Head's pins against `9a31fc992`'s `rule-validator.ts` give 3 failed / 67 passed, exactly the three F3 legs. At head, 70/70. The plugin-security fixture is 18/18.
- **CI at this head:** 41 runs, 36 success, 5 skipped (`Auto Label`, `Check PR Size`, `Build Docs`, `Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`), 0 failures. Every required context is `success`.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/objectql: patch` with `Clause-②: no` still holds. The d.ts is byte-identical to base, the refused set and envelope are unchanged, and one runtime message changes.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Changeset:** every sentence at head is TRUE, including:
- the summary line and the four lead sentences;
- "That refusal is unchanged…" (78 shapes) and the base-text quote;
- the example block, which equals the generated message modulo wrapping;
- the guard bullet (three sentences), the other-reference bullet and the multi-value bullet;
- the reworded "Unchanged" bullet: "a rule that reads a key where it is not held keeps today's text byte for byte, whichever key the fault reports. Those reads are … A declared column always reads, as `null` when empty, so it never counts. …" This is exactly what the code checks.

**Shipped refusal texts at head:** every sentence of the cleared-reference single-value text, the other-reference text and the multi-value text is TRUE (measured).

**PR body, "Patch round 2":** TRUE where measured. "The message differs from base only in the 5 cleanup shapes" is the author's probe count (18 over this review's 78, all the same class). The ablation, suite and gate counts are UNMEASURED here; CI is green.

**"Accepted as is: `record.account.nope`": measured.** Every sentence of its cleanup text is TRUE: the guard lets the delete through, `cascade` / `restrict` behave as said, and the breakage stays loud on every linked write. Base's generic text there names the wrong object. No sentence is false, and it is disclosed in the body.

**The rewritten "How" bullet:** TRUE, except that condition (3), "finds no own read of the rule that faults", is INACCURATE as a description. The function counts an own read of a key its holder lacks whether or not that read faults: `has(record.nope)`, `record.?nope` and `record[?'nope']` count without faulting and keep the generic text. The changeset's own wording ("reads a key where it is not held") is exact, so nothing shipped is false. This is a body-only correction.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-20006-cascade-fk-clear-refusal-text`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Bvd69VPa6puiNzzPUroDBx`

**VERDICT: PASS**

Isolated reviewer: a contract-review-tier subagent, third read on this PR, fed only the card, the two prior records, the PR and AGENTS.md; adopted by the seat.
